notes: Test Valley operates mandatory HMO licensing only. A licence is needed if your property is let to five or more people forming two or more households. There is no selective licensing and no additional HMO licensing anywhere in the borough.
research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE. Test Valley's Private Housing Sector Renewal Policy 2021 (updated April 2022, approved Cabinet 26 May 2021), s.8.2, addresses both limbs by name and rejects both: 'There are discretionary licensing schemes that local authorities may choose to bring into force. The Additional HMO licensing scheme would apply in cases where it is expected that an especially high number of HMOs concentrated in any area would give rise to additional problems. Selective licensing can require any private rented property to have a licence... The adoption of such additional schemes would not be warranted within the Test Valley area currently, although this will be kept under review. Accordingly, at present the Council will operate the mandatory HMO licensing scheme only.' FEE TEST PASSED: the HMO page (Last Updated 17 July 2026) lists 2025/26 and 2026/27 as 'Licence application (up to 5 year licence)' 455.00 / 466.00; 'additional charge per room for HMO above 5 rooms' 25.00; 'Licence renewal' 374.00 / 383.00; Part 2 'Operation charge (HMO licensing scheme)' 249.00; 'Supplementary operation charge' 330.00 / 338.00. No selective fee, no additional-licensing fee, one application route. Page text: 'Since 1st October 2018, any HMO with 5 or more occupants regardless of number of storeys in the property will require a licence.' CONTROLS: the site search is at /newsearch?k= (the ?q= form silently returns an empty shell and was discarded, a methodology trap worth recording). Control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned the HMO pages; nonsense control 'zzqxwvplop' returned 'Sorry, no results matched your search', proving the engine can return zero. 'selective licensing' and 'additional licensing' returned a result set byte-equivalent to bare 'licensing' (taxi, zoo, vehicle, gambling), i.e. the qualifier matched nothing. ModernGov also passed both controls; 'selective licensing' returned one irrelevant alcohol licensing sub-committee annex. No designation report, consultation or Cabinet paper exists. Test Valley has no robots.txt and no sitemap.xml (genuine 404s), so no sitemap sweep was possible; the two control-validated search engines compensate. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Article 4 directions: TVBC has nine since 1972 plus five earlier and EVERY one is a named land parcel (Staddlestone Farm, The Middleway, Land adj Cottage Road Middle Wallop, Wellow Drove, Blackwater Bridge, Allens Copse, Stockbridge Road Timsbury, Newtown Road Awbridge, Upper Clatford, King Lane Over Wallop, plus pre-1972 New Street, Linkenholt Estate, Rooksbury Mill, Castle Lane North Baddesley, Butlers Wood). None is a C3-to-C4 HMO direction, and Article 4 is planning control not licensing in any event. (2) 'additional charge per room for HMO above 5 rooms 25.00' is a per-room surcharge on the mandatory licence. (3) 'Operation charge (HMO licensing scheme)': 'scheme' here means the mandatory regime; it is Part 2 of the two-part mandatory fee. (4) Civil-penalty boilerplate: Appendix 5 of the very policy that says 'mandatory HMO licensing scheme only' lists 'Section 95 (licensing of houses under Part 3)', a statutory offence list copied from the Housing and Planning Act 2016. (5) The Council Tax privacy notice recital, the only other site-wide hit for 'selective': 'Parts 1-4 of the Housing Act 2004 (Housing Conditions, Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation, Selective ...)', a data-protection legal-basis recital. (6) s.254 definition: the page opens 'A property (house or flat) that is occupied by 3 or more people who are from 2 or more households'; the licensable threshold on the same page is five. LIMITATION: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before work began, so all evidence is direct HTTP retrieval with a browser user-agent; no independent index cross-check was possible.

notes: Tewkesbury operates mandatory HMO licensing only. A licence is needed if your property is let to five or more people forming two or more households. There is no selective licensing and no additional HMO licensing anywhere in the borough.
research: NEGATIVE, CONVERGENT rather than declarative; see the confidence note below. The public HMO page states: 'In addition, some HMOs will also require a licence from the council if the property meets the following criteria: Occupied by five or more people, forming two or more households; and Tenants share facilities such as kitchen or bathrooms.' The s.254 definition ('three or more tenants, who form two or more households') is given separately as what an HMO IS, and never makes 3-4 person HMOs licensable. Corroborated on the environmental health housing page: 'The Council is the licensing authority for Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs)', with no other regime named. FEE TEST PASSED: 'Consolidated fee list for 2026/2027 (v.2)', page 5, verbatim under 'HOUSE IN MULTIPLE OCCUPATION (HMO) LICENCES': 'Initial application fee (non-refundable) £336.00'; 'Further fee payable before issue of a licence (successful applications) £864.00'; 'Additional fee for those HMOs wit more than five occupants (additional charge per additional person) £41.00' ('wit' is the council's own typo). Fees were mapped by coordinate extraction rather than naive text order. The word 'selective' appears ZERO times in the entire 10-page consolidated fee list, and the only other housing-related licence block is caravan and mobile home site licensing. SITEMAP SWEEP COMPLETE: /sitemap.xml is a single flat urlset of 965 URLs with all sub-fetches succeeding. Under the licensing-and-permits housing branch there are exactly two children: houses-in-multiple-occupation and caravan-and-mobile-homes-site-licensing. CONTROLS: the WordPress REST site search is BROKEN for negative inference; the nonsense control 'zzqxwv nonsense term' returned 8 results, so it is a fuzzy OR-matcher and a nil result there would prove nothing. No weight was placed on it. ModernGov PASSED both controls (control returned 10 results; 'zzqxwvplop' returned 'No results found'). Its 'selective licensing' hits were all fuzzy matches on 'licensing' alone. The two most relevant committee papers were read in full: the Housing Legislation Report, Executive 31 March 2021, proposes civil penalties only 'for the Regulation of Housing Standards and the Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation'; and the Private Rented Housing Sector Accommodation Fund Pilot, Executive 12 June 2019, a letting-incentive scheme with zero occurrences of 'selective'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Civil-penalty boilerplate: the Draft Civil Penalty Policy lists 'offences in relation to Licensing of houses under Housing Act 2004 Part 3, (Section 95)' adjacent to s.30, s.72, s.139(7) and s.234. (2) Article 4 directions: Tewkesbury's are conservation-area directions (Ashleworth Green, Bishops Cleeve) withdrawing permitted development for 'replacement windows, new fences and walls or domestic extensions'. Nothing to do with HMOs. (3) 'District licensing scheme' under biodiversity is GREAT CRESTED NEWT district licensing under the Conservation of Habitats Regulations. The name is dangerously close to district-wide property licensing and is not it. (4) 'Private lettings scheme - Support for landlords' is a voluntary incentive scheme (£100 finder's fee, deposit paid in full) to source affordable tenancies, the 'selective lettings' trap. (5) The per-person surcharge above five occupants. CONFIDENCE NOTE: unlike Test Valley, Tewkesbury publishes no document saying in terms 'we do not operate selective licensing'. The negative rests on four independent lines: no fee line in the current consolidated schedule, no page in a complete 965-URL sitemap, no committee paper in a control-validated ModernGov search, and an HMO page setting the threshold at five occupants. Sound, but one notch below Test Valley's certainty. LIMITATION: WebSearch budget exhausted before work began. No live consultation on either scheme type was found, and a designation would statutorily require public consultation first.

notes: Three Rivers operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for properties let to five or more people forming two or more households. The council confirmed in January 2026 that it is not introducing additional licensing, and will review that in 2027. No selective licensing.
research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE, WITH A LIVE REVIEW COMMITMENT. This council came closest in the batch to a genuine positive and was resolved against primary committee papers. TWO DECISIVE SOURCES. (1) TRDC's own HMO Licensing Policy, April 2026 (approved Policy and Resources Committee 29 June 2026), section 5 'Types of Licensing': s.5.2 Additional Licensing, 'At the time of adopting this policy, Three Rivers District Council does not operate an Additional Licensing scheme, however reserve the right to adopt Additional Licensing at any point if required. This position will be reviewed every 12 months.' s.5.3 Selective Licensing, 'At the time of adopting this policy, Three Rivers District Council does not operate a Selective Licensing scheme, however reserve the right to adopt Selective Licensing at any point where evidence demonstrates it would address local housing problems.' Section 4 confirms scope: 'Under the mandatory licensing scheme currently operated by the council, a property must be licensed... Is occupied by five or more people / Forms two or more households / Shares basic amenities.' (2) Policy and Resources Committee, 26 January 2026, item PR1424 'REVIEW OF HMO ADDITIONAL LICENCING AND CONSIDERATION OF ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION'. The printed minutes record RESOLVED: 'Based on evidence at this time, additional licensing for HMOs is not progressed, however, this will be reviewed in 12 months' time. Based on evidence at this time, that an Article 4 direction is not progressed...' A Cooper/Edwards amendment to replace 'is not progressed' with 'is progressed' on both limbs was PUT TO THE VOTE AND LOST, For 4, Against 8, Abstention 1. IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: the narrative section of those same minutes contains the loose phrase 'HMOs... were already regulated through the Council's additional licensing scheme'. This is minute-taker error, resolved against the officer report in the supplementary agenda, which states at 3.1.9 'The council currently operate a mandatory HMO licensing scheme' and at 3.1.16 'it is the Officer recommendation that at this current time any progression with additional licensing by the council would currently be disproportionate and premature.' The report records only 13 licensed HMOs in the district and notes 'no other local authority located within Hertfordshire has introduced additional licensing'. HISTORY: Full Council on 21 October 2025 asked officers to review 'an additional licencing scheme, which would require landlords of small HMOs occupied by less than five occupants to apply to the council for a licence', which produced the January 2026 decision. Explored, formally declined, no consultation, no fee. RE-CHECK around January to April 2027 when the 12-month review falls due. FEE TEST: TRDC's 'Licensing Fees 2026-2027' contains no property or HMO licensing fees at all; its headings are Hackney Carriage and Private Hire, Sex Establishment, Street trading, Premises Licence, Club Premises Certificate, TEN, Personal Licence, gaming permits, Small Society Lottery, Scrap Metal, Pavement Licence and Hypnotism. CONTROLS: TRDC's own site search is BROKEN; the control, real and nonsense queries all returned the same ~318KB client-rendered page with an identical default listing (similarity of nonsense vs real query 0.9995). The on-site meetings archive is STALE, ending 30 April 2023, and 2026 meeting URLs return a soft-404 catch-all listing rather than a 404 status. The live committee system is moderngov.threerivers.gov.uk (threerivers.moderngov.co.uk and democracy.threerivers.gov.uk do not resolve); its document search PASSED controls. Sitemap sweep of sitemap-0.xml (2,773 URLs) found exactly one HMO service page. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) LIVE DISTRICT-WIDE ARTICLE 4 CONSULTATION, the exact look-alike: 'Article 4 Direction - Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) District wide', agreed at Policy and Resources 1 June 2026, representations by 16 August 2026, in force about 12 months later. It is PLANNING: 'The Direction will require an application to be made to the council for the grant of planning permission before a property can be developed into an HMO.' (2) A 2022 Article 4 Direction (effective 29 March 2024) covers Class E to C3 commercial-to-residential, unrelated to HMOs. (3) s.254 definition on the landing page versus the stated mandatory threshold of five. (4) 'Additional fee' lines in the fee PDF are a premises licence surcharge for events of 5,000+ attendance; 'Additional site 649.00' is Scrap Metal Dealers Act. (5) 'decision made by a designated officer under delegated authority' is officer delegation, not a s.56 or s.80 designation. (6) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: TRDC shares services with Watford BC; every source relied on is TRDC's own. LIMITATION: WebSearch budget exhausted. No expired designation was found and none is referenced in any policy or committee paper.

notes: Tonbridge and Malling states it only operates mandatory HMO licensing, for properties let to five or more people forming two or more households. There is no selective licensing and no additional HMO licensing in the borough.
research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE. Primary source, under the heading 'Licensing HMOs': 'We only operate mandatory licensing of HMOs that meet one of the first three tests above and where the property is occupied by five or more people made up of more than one household. A mandatory HMO licence is not required for self-contained flats in purpose built blocks of three or more flats.' The word 'only' is the council's own. FEE TEST PASSED, verbatim from the same page: 'Fees from 1 April 2026 are as follows: new HMO licence - £810; renewal HMO licence - £727'. One licence type, one route, no discretionary cost-recovery fee. Historic fee decisions use the same framing: Communities and Housing Advisory Board 14 Nov 2016 and Cabinet 9 Feb 2017 set 'fees and charges in respect of the mandatory licensing scheme for Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) and Caravan Sites'. CORROBORATION: the Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy 2022, p.14: 'The Housing Act 2004 introduced a mandatory scheme to licence HMOs, and this was extended in 2018 to include an HMO occupied by five or more people, comprising two or more households...' No other licensing scheme is described anywhere in its 40 pages. INDEPENDENT RAW-HTML CHECK: all five pages of the landlords and tenants guide were fetched with a browser user-agent and grepped in RAW HTML (not rendered text) for 'selective' and 'additional licen': zero occurrences on every page. Sitemap (2,651 URLs) contains no selective or additional licensing page; the only HMO entries are the licence guide, the HMO licensing privacy notice, HMO amenity standards guidance and a Local Plan policy H9 consultation response. Note the bare host tmbc.gov.uk does not resolve; www.tmbc.gov.uk returns 200. CONTROLS: the real search endpoint is /site-search/results/?q= (the /search?q= form 404s). PASSED both ways: control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 23 genuine results, 'selective licensing' 18, and nonsense 'zqxwvpjklmqq' returned ZERO results with the page shrinking from ~56KB to ~36KB. The engine demonstrably returns zero, so its nil findings carry weight; it also indexes ModernGov documents. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Civil-penalty boilerplate, the decisive one here: the only 'selective licensing' text in the 2022 enforcement policy is the s.249A relevant-housing-offences recital, 'Failing to licence a house subject to selective licensing under Part 3 (section 95(1))' and 'Failing to comply with the condition of a selective licence issued under Part 3'. That list recites every offence in the Act regardless of which schemes the authority operates. Also para 1.1.36, harm-categorisation guidance. (2) Article 4 Direction scoping report, Housing and Planning Scrutiny Select Committee 19 May 2026, item 22: planning not licensing, AND not made: 'the evidence base within the Borough was limited... the Council's Strategic Housing Market Assessment did not support the introduction of an Article 4 Direction at this stage.' Further evidence work approved subject to about £25,000 funding, with 'Cabinet make a decision on the Article 4 Direction no later than their meeting on 1 September 2026'. Worth re-checking after that date, but it can only ever create a planning requirement, never a licence. (3) Every 'additional licensing' search hit was a Licensing and Appeals Committee page or the Statement of Licensing Policy 2025-2030. (4) The consultations page lists only a closed alcohol licensing policy consultation. (5) s.254 definition: the page sets out the Standard test, Self-contained flat test and Converted building test as what an HMO IS, then separately states the five-person threshold. LIMITATIONS: ModernGov's native mgSearchResults.aspx returns 'Error - page unavailable', so committee papers were searched via the council site search, which passed controls and did surface ModernGov PDFs and decision records; good coverage but not exhaustive. A 2006 Cabinet report 'Housing Act 2004' mentions selective licensing and could not be retrieved (302 cross-host redirect); immaterial, because any 2006 designation would have expired by 2011 at the latest and every current source states mandatory-only. WebSearch budget exhausted before work began.

notes: Torbay operates mandatory HMO licensing only. A licence is needed if your property is let to five or more people forming two or more households; Torbay confirms a four-occupant share is not licensable. There is no selective or additional licensing.
research: NEGATIVE. Flagged for extra scrutiny as a coastal unitary with large bedsit stock in Torquay and Paignton; checked hard and cleared. FEE TEST PASSED, the entire housing licensing fee schedule verbatim: 'HMO licences last up to 5 years and have two payment parts: Part 1: Processing the application (non-refundable); Part 2: Managing the licence (paid after approval)... New application £2,007 (£485 / £1,522); New application (enforced) £2,859; Renewal application £1,709 (£428 / £1,281); Renewal application (enforced) £2,054.' There is no selective licence fee and no additional-HMO licence fee anywhere on the site, and applications are made via the single GOV.UK mandatory route. THRESHOLD TEST, INDEPENDENTLY DECISIVE: the council's 'quickly check if your property is an HMO' page gives worked examples: 'A house occupied by 5 students (2 of whom are living together), who share a kitchen and bathroom. Licensable because there are 5 occupiers in 4 households sharing basic amenities.' and 'Two bedroom bungalow shared by 2 couples. Not licensable because there are only 4 occupiers.' Under an additional licensing designation a 4-occupant, 2-household share WOULD be licensable; Torbay states positively that it is not. This also resolves the ambiguously-worded trap on the apply page ('To rent out an HMO, you need a licence'), exactly as with the Tendring precedent. The 'what is an HMO' page names exactly one scheme: 'Mandatory HMO licensing scheme. From 1 October 2018 mandatory licensing is no longer limited to certain HMOs that are 3 or more storeys high...'. RAW-HTML SWEEP: 11 housing and landlord pages grepped in raw HTML: 'selective' 0, 'additional' 0, 'designat' 0. CONTROLS: site search PASSED both ways; control returned 124 results, nonsense returned 'Your search did not match any documents', and 'selective licensing' returned ONE document, a procurement page 'How we invite bids and select suppliers', a stem match on 'select'. Note /sitemap.xml 404s while the bare /sitemap returns 200 with 5,825 URLs; that sweep found only HMO-landlord pages. COMMITTEE PAPERS: the mgSearchResults.aspx path does not exist and returns a byte-identical 5,074-byte 404 for every query INCLUDING the control, which would have been a false nil; the working endpoint is ieSearchResults.aspx via POST. That PASSED controls (16 document hits vs 0 for nonsense, with a distinct response size). The exact phrase 'selective licensing' returns 5 documents in Torbay's ENTIRE committee history, latest 2012: a 2012 scrutiny review recommending 'That targeted selective and/or additional licensing of houses in multiple occupation be prioritised', and the Mayoral Record of Decision of 14 June 2012 in which that recommendation was NOT accepted, being deferred to a service review and budget prioritisation 'as additional resources will be required.' Never designated, and absent from committee papers in the 14 years since. MOST RECENT PRIMARY SOURCE, 13 months before verification: Cabinet 14 July 2025, 'Housing Standards Civil Penalty Policy and HMO Licence Conditions Review', a full review describing only mandatory licensing. CORROBORATION: the Housing Strategy 2023-2030 contains zero occurrences of 'licen' or 'HMO'; the HMO register (last updated July 2026) holds 144 licensed properties, consistent with mandatory-only, whereas an additional scheme across Torquay and Paignton would produce many hundreds. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Article 4, and a correction to the working assumption: Torbay does NOT have an HMO Article 4 direction. Its statutory MHCLG dataset holds exactly two records, Polsham (11 April 2002) and Churston (5 November 1998), both conservation-area directions. A bay-wide C3-to-C4 HMO Article 4 was PROPOSED to Council on 16 May 2012 but does not appear in the adopted dataset. (2) Civil-penalty boilerplate: the single 2025 hit is 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses under Part 3 [section 95]'. (3) 'Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007' is the s.257 statutory instrument, not s.56. (4) Cabinet Appendix 3 'List of additional conditions for Torbay HMO's' is extra conditions on mandatory licences. (5) s.254 definition versus the stated threshold of five. (6) All 'additional licensing' hits were taxi, private hire, alcohol, club premises, gambling permits and leaflet distribution. (7) Torbay's voluntary Landlord Accreditation Scheme was closed to new applicants from July 2012. WARD NAMES: not applicable; no designation has ever been made, so no ward or area list exists. LIMITATIONS: WebSearch budget exhausted. ModernGov's date-range filter is server-side broken (StartDate/EndDate POST params ignored), compensated by verifying the index covers 2025-2026 material and reading dates off each hit. ModernGov default search is fuzzy OR-matching, so quoted exact phrases were used.

notes: Torridge operates mandatory HMO licensing only. A licence is needed if your property is let to five or more people forming two or more households. Torridge notes a property can be an HMO without needing a licence. No selective or additional licensing.
research: NEGATIVE. Treated as elevated risk because Torridge is coastal (Bideford, Northam, Westward Ho!) and coastal towns with bedsit stock are where designations cluster; cleared on primary evidence. PRIMARY SOURCE, the only HMO licensing page, verbatim: 'HMO Licences - With effect from 1st October 2018, The Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Prescribed Description) (England) Order 2018... Its effect is that mandatory licensing will apply to HMOs that are below three storeys (as well as to those of three or more storeys) where the property: is occupied by 5 or more persons; and is occupied by persons living in two or more separate households; and who share an amenity such as a kitchen, toilet, bathroom or lounge'. And decisively: 'A property that is classed as an HMO does not necessarily need licensing, but is still an HMO.' That sentence is incompatible with any additional licensing designation. The only application route is the GOV.UK mandatory route. INDEPENDENT RAW-HTML CHECK of that page: zero occurrences of 'selective' or 'additional licen'. FEE TEST PASSED: 'Fees and Charges 2026-27'. The entire Housing section contains these and only these licensing lines: 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Licence / Part A - Application Fee (Plus DBS Fee) / Part B - Grant Fee (Management and Enforcement) / Renewal' and 'HMO Licence Variation / Inspection required / No Inspection required'. 2026/27 values against the HMO licence rows are £341.00 (Part A) and £787.00 (Part B). CAVEAT: this PDF's text layer misaligns its price columns, so the label set is authoritative and the individual figures are indicative. There is no selective and no additional licensing fee anywhere in the schedule. CONTROLS: Torridge's site search PASSED both ways; control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 376 loose hits, nonsense 'zzqqxwplop' returned 'found no results', and 'designation' returned 227 hits with genuine neighbourhood-plan results, proving the engine indexes that term. Against that working engine: 'selective licensing' no results; 'additional licensing' no results; 'selective licence' no results; 'licensing scheme' one result (Boat and Skipper licences). SITEMAP SWEEP: 2,032 URLs, independently retrieved and grepped; the only HMO URL in the entire estate is /hmos, and every other 'licen' URL is boat skipper, animal welfare, scrap metal, caravan and camping, gambling, taxi or alcohol licensing. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) The 'HMO Licensing Scope and Schemes' PDF, the most dangerous item here. Its title reads like a designation and it contains a full section headed 'Additional Licensing Schemes'. It is a generic statutory explainer, 'An LHA can make an additional licensing scheme...', signed off 'Produced by Environwest (UK) Ltd for Torridge District Council January 2007'. Pure statutory-powers recital. (2) The Housing Enforcement Policy May 2026: 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act 2004]' sits inside a bulleted list headed 'The Council has the power to impose a Civil Financial Penalty for the following'. (3) The housing-regulation page: 'Failure to obtain a selective HMO licence [S.95(1)]', again inside a list of offences the team CAN investigate. (4) Article 4 Directions: conservation-area and heritage permitted-development control, returned alongside Conservation Areas and the Local Heritage List. (5) s.254 definition wording versus the stated threshold of five. LIMITATION, THE ONE GENUINE GAP: the ModernGov committee search FAILED its control; it returned nothing for any multi-word phrase and nothing for 'HMO', while 'housing' did return 5 results, i.e. the index responds but not consistently, and the ieSearchResults POST was tried across DocType 0-4. NO INFERENCE, POSITIVE OR NEGATIVE, SHOULD BE DRAWN FROM TORRIDGE COMMITTEE PAPERS. The negative rests on the fee-schedule test, the explicit 'does not necessarily need licensing' wording, a complete sitemap sweep and a control-validated site search returning zero for every phrase variant. WebSearch budget was exhausted before work began.

notes: Trafford operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for properties let to five or more people forming two or more households. There is no selective licensing and no additional HMO licensing. Trafford has a borough-wide Article 4 direction, which is planning control, not licensing.
research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE. Flagged as a metropolitan borough between Manchester and Salford, both of which do run schemes; cleared on five converging primary sources. STRONGEST SINGLE SOURCE: Trafford's own completed DLUHC return, 'Local authority returns form: damp and mould in private rented properties', issued after the Secretary of State's letter of 19 November 2022 and published as an appendix to Council papers. Q1 'Please provide the full name of your local authority:' - 'Trafford Borough Council'. Q6 'Do you run any Selective and/or Additional Licensing schemes in your area?' - 'Neither'. Q7 'If you do run any licensing schemes, approximately how many properties are covered?' - 'N/A'. Source: democratic.trafford.gov.uk, Council 20 March 2024. SECOND: Executive report 27 November 2017, para 1.11, explicitly rules selective licensing out: 'Latest available data confirms that there is only one ward where this level is exceeded for private rented property, Priory Ward. Currently there is no evidence base for Priory ward which identifies that the criteria for selective licensing are being exceeded. This in itself means that we cannot consider Selective Private Sector Licensing.' Priory Ward is named ONLY as the ward meeting the private-rented-proportion precondition; NO DESIGNATION WAS EVER MADE, so it must not be rendered as a scheme or a ward list. FEE TEST PASSED, complete table verbatim: 'Fee on application for a licence £1012 up to and including 6 bedrooms, plus an additional fee of £25 for every bedroom thereafter'; 'Fee on granting of a licence £211'; 'Application to vary licence £331'; 'Pre-licence application advice £435'. One licence route, one fee stream. SCOPE PAGE: 'A property will require a mandatory HMO licence if it is rented to five or more people from more than one household', and no additional or selective tier appears anywhere in the 8-page HMO guide. The public register (Dec 2025) holds 76 licensed HMOs with NO licence-type column, consistent with a single mandatory regime. CONTROLS: the council site search uses parameter search_api_fulltext; the obvious 'search' parameter is silently inert, a methodology trap worth recording. Control returned the HMO page, SPD6 and Article 4 Directions; negative control 'zzqxwvnonsenseterm' returned 'No items to show', proving it can return zero. COMMITTEE PAPERS: the live system is democratic.trafford.gov.uk. Note trafford.moderngov.co.uk returns Cloudflare 522 (origin down) and democracy.trafford.gov.uk does not resolve; a 522 is not evidence. democratic.trafford.gov.uk PASSED both controls. Six differently-worded queries returned only planning applications, conservation-area appraisals, taxi licensing, climate reports and the enforcement policy. SITEMAP SWEEP: a two-part index (lastmod 2026-08-05), 2,704 URLs, 'selective' zero and 'additional.{0,3}licen' zero. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Article 4 Direction, borough-wide, and Trafford does have one, removing permitted development rights for C3-to-C4 conversion, introduced because of University Academy 92: 'There is an Article 4 Direction in place across Trafford that relates to Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs).' It triggers a PLANNING APPLICATION, never a licence. (2) s.95 civil-penalty and RRO boilerplate in the Place Directorate Enforcement Policy 2025, which alone generated 3 of about 11 committee hits. (3) The per-bedroom surcharge. (4) s.254 definition versus the threshold of five on the very next page. (5) 'Selective schools': the same 20 March 2024 Council document discusses grammar-school admissions ('All Trafford Selective Schools'). (6) Housing Allocation Policy 2025, the 'selective lettings' trap. (7) A grep hit for 'S56' on the HMO page proved on inspection to be random base64 noise inside a JavaScript blob, not a statutory reference, a direct illustration of why raw HTML must be read in context. (8) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing from Manchester or Salford was relied on. No expired scheme was found and no trace exists in committee records back to 2013; the 2017 wording 'we cannot consider' indicates none had ever been made. LIMITATIONS: WebSearch budget exhausted. ModernGov result pagination did not respond to a Page parameter, so the top 10 per query across six differently-worded queries were reviewed rather than an exhaustive list.

notes: Tunbridge Wells operates mandatory HMO licensing only. A licence is needed if your property is let to five or more people forming two or more households. Licence fees start at the five-occupant band. There is no selective or additional HMO licensing.
research: NEGATIVE. PRIMARY SOURCE, verbatim: 'HMO licensing - HMOs must be licensed where they are occupied by five persons or more in two or more households. This includes any HMO which is a building or a converted flat where householders share amenities such as a toilet, personal washing facilities or cooking facilities.' And: 'HMO standards - Whether your HMO needs a licence or not, it must meet our HMO standards.' The second sentence expressly contemplates unlicensed HMOs, which is incompatible with an additional licensing designation. FEE TEST PASSED, and this is the strongest single item, same page verbatim: 'Licence fee - We have reviewed our HMO licensing fee structure and made some changes... From 1 April 2026, the fees are as follows: Occupancy / Licence fee - 5-7 occupants £813 - 8 or more occupants £908'. And renewals '5-7 occupants £701 - 8 or more occupants £748'. THE FEE LADDER STARTS AT FIVE OCCUPANTS. There is no band for 3-4 occupants, which an additional scheme would necessarily need, and no per-dwelling selective fee. The structure was reviewed as recently as 1 April 2026, so it is current and not a stale page. RAW-HTML FORENSICS: this page was grepped in raw HTML rather than rendered text; zero hits for 'selective', 'additional licen' and 'designat', and zero base64 blobs (specifically checked for the encoded-in-JavaScript pattern that concealed an answer on Sunderland). STRUCTURAL SWEEPS, used because the site search is unusable: (a) the A-Z index is server-rendered and complete; the only dwelling-licensing entry is 'Licensing of houses in multiple occupation', and there is no 'Selective licensing' or 'Additional licensing' entry. (b) the HTML sitemap is comprehensive with 65 housing links; the control 'multiple occupation' is present exactly once and 'selective' and 'additional licen' zero times. (c) the Have Your Say page contains zero mentions of HMO, multiple occupation, selective or additional licensing, so there is no live consultation. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) The civil penalty policy for landlords: 'offences in relation to licensing of houses under Part 3 of the Act (section 95 Housing Act 2004)' appears in the s.249A list of offences for which a penalty MAY be imposed. (2) s.254 definition on the HMO page: 'An HMO is defined as a building... which is let to three or more persons forming two or more households'; the same page sets the licensing threshold at five. (3) 'Planning legislation - Where there are more than six tenants planning permission is required' is planning (sui generis), not licensing. (4) Article 4 Directions: these are PROPERTY-SPECIFIC directions on named premises (7 Vale Avenue, Angel Food and Wine, Apple Pie Farm, Bidborough Stores, Brokes Wood, Brunch Cafe, Cadogan House and others). Not a district-wide HMO C3-to-C4 direction. (5) Caravan site licensing and the fit and proper person register are Caravan Sites Act and Mobile Homes Act 2013 regimes. LIMITATIONS, STATED PLAINLY: (a) WebFetch is bot-blocked (HTTP 403); worked around with curl plus a browser user-agent, which returned 200, and the 403 was not treated as evidence. www.tunbridgewells.gov.uk redirects to the bare host. (b) The XML sitemap sits behind a Cloudflare interstitial, so the server-rendered HTML sitemap and the A-Z were substituted; both are complete. (c) The site search is a client-side Cludo widget and is UNUSABLE over HTTP; control, real and nonsense queries all returned a byte-identical 50,373-byte shell. Not relied on. (d) THE ONE GENUINE GAP: the ModernGov committee search FAILED its control, returning 'No results found' even for the single word 'licensing', across DocType 0-4. NO INFERENCE SHOULD BE DRAWN FROM TUNBRIDGE WELLS COMMITTEE PAPERS EITHER WAY. The negative rests on the fee-schedule test, the explicit 'whether your HMO needs a licence or not' wording, the complete A-Z and HTML sitemap sweeps, and the absence of any consultation on Have Your Say. A designation consulted on but not yet fee-bearing would not be caught by the fee test alone, which is why Have Your Say was checked separately. (e) WebSearch budget exhausted.

notes: Wakefield operates mandatory HMO licensing only, for properties let to five or more people forming two or more households. There is no selective licensing; the council decided against it in 2021. Article 4 rules in some areas are planning control, not licensing.
research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE. Flagged as a metropolitan borough with a plausible ward-based designation; cleared on primary committee evidence, independently retrieved and read in full. THE COUNCIL'S OWN WORDS: scrutiny report to the Regeneration, Employment and Skills Overview and Scrutiny Committee, 24 November 2021 ('WARDS AFFECTED: ALL'), para 5.3: 'Properties rented out in England are not currently registered or licensed and landlords do not need to declare that they own or manage property, unless they have a house in multiple occupation with 5 or more occupants or there is an additional or selective licensing scheme in place in their local arear. There is currently no selective licensing scheme in the Wakefield District.' FORMALLY REJECTED: the minutes record 'Resolved - (1) Based on the information received and after careful consideration the Committee feels that on balance both a district wide and/or selective licensing would not be the best strategy for Wakefield to manage the private rented sector at the present time. (2) The Committee supports the view that there are less expensive and better focused ways of tackling any private rented sector issues. However, the Committee believes that selective licensing is something that should be kept under review should the circumstances change.' The briefing was explicit that this was Part 3, and officers stated Wakefield fails the entry tests: 'Wakefield does not have low demand, indeed the private rented sector was strong and properties were at a premium.' An indicative fee of 'around £750-£1000 for each privately rented property' was discussed but never adopted. 'selective licensing designation' returns only 3 results across the entire committee archive back to 2003, the sole relevant one being the November 2021 minutes; the remaining hits are Internal Audit Plans from 2004 to 2014 matching the audit phrase 'selective areas of activity'. notes: Warrington states it has no plans to introduce additional or selective licensing anywhere in the borough. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for properties let to five or more people forming two or more households.
research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE, TWICE OVER. Flagged as a unitary with central wards where a designation was plausible; cleared. EXPLICIT COUNCIL STATEMENT: the council's 'HMO licensing - further information' PDF lists all three Housing Act 2004 licensing types under headings '2. Additional Licensing' and '3. Selective Licensing of other residential accommodation', then states verbatim: 'Warrington Borough Council has no plans to introduce Additional or Selective Licensing anywhere within the Borough.' SECOND, CURRENT GUIDANCE (HMO Guidance May 2024): 'If you operate a HMO with 5 or more people living in it, who live together as 2 or more households then it must be licensed... There is another type of licensing known as Selective Licensing but this is not carried out in this authority at present.' FEE TEST PASSED, the complete Housing standards section of 'Fees and Charges 2026-2027' (page updated 7 April 2026): 'House in multiple occupation (HMO) / Fee (exc VAT): New licence £492.09; Licence with CLAS membership (10% reduction) £442.87; Licence for charitable organisation (50% reduction) £246.04; Licence variation £47.44'. Followed only by Immigration inspection, 'Notices - Housing act 2004 £382.86' and Caravan sites. Independent raw-HTML greps of four housing pages returned ZERO occurrences of 'selective licensing' or 'additional licensing'. ADDITIONAL LICENSING EXPRESSLY REJECTED AT CABINET, 8 September 2025, Agenda Item 8, para 6.18: 'It is not considered at present that the designation of discretionary additional licensing areas within the central area could be justified, because currently there is little evidence that the Borough's HMOs are consistently badly managed.' Para 5.1 confirms the threshold: 'There are currently 211 licensed Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) in Warrington. Any HMOs operating without a licence (i.e operating with fewer than five residents) are not reflected.' Cabinet's recommendation was an Article 4 Direction only. The Housing Policy Committee (30 July 2025) had offered additional licensing as an optional extra at para 12.3, but its formal recommendations were Article 4 plus SPD only, and Cabinet did not take the licensing option. HISTORIC CONSIDERATION, NO DESIGNATION EVER MADE: CMIS returned 23 documents for 'selective licensing', spanning 25 June 2013 to 4 March 2015 ONLY, nothing later. Building Stronger Communities Policy Committee, 9 July 2014 minutes: 'The findings of the group were that there was not a case currently for selective licensing in Warrington but the item could be revisited when Government Guidelines became available.' Work programme monitoring through March 2015 repeats: 'there was not a satisfactory case for selective licensing in Warrington at the present time'. No designation was ever made, so there is no start or end date to report. SITEMAP SWEEP: all 1,439 URLs independently retrieved and grepped; no housing-related licensing URL beyond the HMO page, and no URL containing 'selective'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, the critical one, and it is brand new: 'On 13 May 2026 Warrington Borough Council... confirmed a without immediate effect Article 4 Direction, under Article 4(1) of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015... applies to the Central Six Wards of the Borough consisting of Orford, Poplars and Hulme, Fairfield and Howley, Latchford East, Latchford West, and Bewsey and Whitecross, and will come into force on 25 September 2026.' Cabinet then approved a BOROUGH-WIDE extension on 9 June 2026 alongside a new HMO Supplementary Planning Document. This is PLANNING CONTROL, NOT LICENSING. (2) The HMO Supplementary Planning Document. (3) Cheshire Landlord Accreditation Scheme (CLAS) 10% fee discount, voluntary accreditation. (4) 'The council may also apply additional conditions to the license', licence conditions not s.56. (5) s.254 definition versus the threshold of five. (6) Application form boilerplate 'Whether this application for an HMO licence under Part 2 or for a house licence under Part 3 of the Housing Act 2004', national model-form wording. (7) The Private Rented Sector Access Scheme, homelessness and tenancy access. (8) Caravan site licence fees and the £382.86 enforcement notice charge. (9) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: Liverpool and Halton excluded. COMMERCIAL WARNING WORTH SURFACING: several non-council aggregators currently assert Warrington operates selective licensing in 'Latchford, Fairfield and Howley, and Bewsey and Whitecross'. That is EXACTLY the Article 4 ward list. Competitors have mistaken the planning direction for a licensing scheme and are publishing a wrong answer; none was relied on here. WARD BOUNDARY POSITION: Warrington did NOT have new wards at the 2024 elections. The LGBCE electoral review is live now, with final recommendations December 2026 and 'electoral arrangements to be implemented for the May 2028 local elections'. The six Article 4 ward names above are therefore current and stable until May 2028. LIMITATIONS: (a) The council's own website search is BROKEN and proves nothing either way; the control returned '4041 results found' and the nonsense negative control returned the IDENTICAL 4041 results, i.e. it returns the whole index regardless of query. A full sitemap sweep was used instead. (b) CMIS search was validated with controls and is sound. (c) CMIS full-text indexing appears thinner before 2013, so a pre-2013 designation cannot be excluded from CMIS alone, but the 2013-2015 papers uniformly frame the question as whether to INTRODUCE a scheme, the council's own PDF says it has 'no plans to introduce' one, and any such designation could not be live now given the five-year statutory maximum. (d) warrington.moderngov.co.uk returns Cloudflare 522 and democracy.warrington.gov.uk does not resolve; the live committee system is cmis.warrington.gov.uk. (e) WebSearch budget exhausted.
